messages:
support_engineer: @oncall_sre Heads-up: customer ACME reported sharp p99 spike starting 18:02 UTC — from ~200ms to ~2.4s, ~12% 5xx timeouts. They provided request IDs and a short trace. Link: https://metrics.redwood.example/shot/abc123 :eyes:

oncall_sre: grabbing traces. Any signs in admission metrics? admit_rejected, admit_queue_depth, inflight_slots?

support_engineer: quick dump from their request header: tenant acme-1, route /v1/generate, model rdx-small. They saw many requests with status code 524 and codepath stuck at "admitting". I pulled our dashboard: admit_queue_depth jumped from ~5 -> ~280 between 18:01-18:06. inflight_per_worker is saturated.

eng_runtime: looks like a worker-side saturation scenario. Recent deploy 17:58 had batching changes (auto-batch-size increased). Could be causing long tail while batches wait for fill. @devops-bot can you show worker CPU/GPU util and RPC latencies for 17:55-18:10?

devops-bot: metrics snapshot attached. GPU util steady ~78%, CPU spiking on router process, rpc_latency_median 8ms -> 230ms for GetBatch calls, worker_conn_queue_len spiked.

priya_pm: customer impact: ACME reports production errors for realtime chat. They're asking for ETA on mitigation.

oncall_sre: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) reduce max_auto_batch_size on rdx-small pool to avoid long wait for batch fill 2) temporarily raise max_concurrency for acme-1 (tenant override) 3) enable fast-fail frontend policy for small requests. Which is lowest-risk?

eng_runtime: safest first: reduce batch timeout and max_auto_batch_size in runtime config. Patch candidate:
```
# runtime config patch
model_pools.rdx-small.max_auto_batch_size: 8 -> 4
model_pools.rdx-small.batch_wait_ms: 10 -> 2
```
Apply to canary pool first (canary-pool-2). Then if stable, roll to all.

support_engineer: adding customer -> informing them we're investigating and trying a quick patch. They've been asked to hold requests for 5m if possible.

oncall_sre: rolled to canary-pool-2 at 18:09. Observing admit_queue_depth for canary: immediate drop from 260 -> 22, rpc_latency for GetBatch down to 20-30ms. Will monitor for 10m.

customer_janet: thanks for quick response. We're seeing immediate improvement on our side, p99 dropping to ~350ms. Holding on further changes pending your update. :pray:

eng_runtime: prom query used during triage: `sum(rate(admit_queue_depth[1m])) by (pool)` and `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(worker_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))` — both were useful. Found correlation with an A/B microconfig that bumped batch target for rdx-small for low qps tenants. Rolling that back for acme-1 too.

oncall_sre: follow-up: after 12m, global admit_queue_depth stabilized under 30, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~380ms. Marking mitigation as successful. Next steps:
- eng_runtime to revert the auto-batch A/B change and add guardrail to prevent oversized batch waits for low-qps tenants (owner: @eng_runtime)
- platform to add a tenant-level emergency concurrency override runbook (owner: @oncall_sre)
- support to notify ACME about root cause and timeline for a permanent fix (owner: @support_engineer)

eng_runtime: created PR with guardrail + unit tests. Also adding telemetry: `batch_wait_time_by_tenant` and `batch_fill_rate` so we can alert on growing waits.

priya_pm: please include impact summary and customer remediation steps for the postmortem. Also check billing implications if we temporarily increased concurrency.

support_engineer: sending ACME update now. Draft note: "We saw transient request pile-up caused by a batching configuration that increased wait time for small-volume tenants. We applied a canary patch reducing batch size + wait, which restored latency. We will roll a permanent guardrail to prevent reoccurrence."

oncall_sre: closing the live incident. Tagging for postmortem. Good job team :tada:
